source_snapshot.procedure: Confirm the SUT recipe, clear logs, follow the installation guideline to install a CPU in the motherboard socket, verify CPU size/socket compatibility, and check that the setup menu displays CPU information; then collect results/photos and unexpected logs.
source_snapshot.criteria: CPU size follows the specification and can be installed in the motherboard
source_snapshot.deepseek_finding: Installing a physical CPU, handling the socket and thermal interface, and verifying the board require an on-site person and cannot be performed over SSH.

original_test_intent.purpose: Physically install the exact approved processor into its designated motherboard socket, prove package/keying/retention compatibility without damage, and verify that the firmware setup menu recognizes and displays the installed CPU information.
original_test_intent.target: One identified motherboard/socket/revision and one owner-approved CPU model/stepping/package in the required population position; not an arbitrary socket-compatible processor or another CPU discovered remotely.
original_test_intent.scope: One qualified ESD-safe CPU installation using the exact board/socket procedure, required thermal-interface and retention steps, followed by approved power-on and recognition in the named firmware setup menu. BMC/OS inventory is supporting health evidence, not a substitute for the setup-menu observation.
original_test_intent.operation: Preserve the pre-state, isolate power, have a qualified operator inspect the socket/CPU, orient and install the CPU with approved tools/TIM/retention sequence and no force, restore the thermal/chassis assembly, perform the approved first power-on under KVM/OOB recovery coverage, capture the firmware setup CPU page, and collect post-install boot/thermal/power/log evidence.
original_test_intent.duration_and_iterations: One CPU installation and one approved first power-on/firmware-setup recognition check; the source lists five attended and zero machine minutes, which is not a credible authorization to shorten the physical or first-boot procedure.
original_test_intent.expected_result: The correct CPU fits and locks into the specified socket with no pin/contact, package, retention or TIM anomaly; the board powers on safely; the required firmware setup page reports the expected CPU identity/topology; and no disallowed thermal, power, boot, BMC or log fault appears.
original_test_intent.required_evidence: SUT/board/socket and CPU part/serial/stepping/package identity, approved compatibility/population/install guide, operator/ESD/tool/TIM record, before/after socket and installed-state photos, retention/thermal assembly evidence, firmware setup screen with CPU information, first-boot/POST, temperature/power, BMC/SEL and recovery evidence.
ambiguities: The source does not identify the CPU, package, socket/board revision, population rule, BIOS support, installation guide, torque/tool/TIM requirements or expected setup-menu fields.
The five-minute attended and zero-minute machine values do not define safe installation, power-on or recognition timing.

v2_review_conclusion.finding: V2 correctly requires a qualified operator, exact CPU/board/socket/BIOS/TIM/ESD inputs, no-force handling, OOB recovery and before/after health. It sometimes groups BIOS, BMC and OS recognition together, while the source specifically requires CPU information in the setup menu; only that named firmware view is mandatory acceptance evidence.

applicable_history.decision: The prior one-by-one review retained physical/manual execution and operator evidence for the CPU installation case.

v3_review_conclusion.summary: The physical CPU installation remains MANUAL ONLY. V3 narrows the mandatory recognition location to the source-required firmware setup menu and keeps BMC/OS inventory as supporting evidence, while preserving V2's ESD, socket, thermal, power and recovery controls.

available_now: The source clearly requires physical CPU installation, mechanical compatibility and firmware setup-menu recognition.
Read-only board/firmware/current-CPU/BMC inventory and existing logs can be preserved before the chassis is opened.
missing_inputs: Exact SUT, board/socket revision, CPU model/stepping/package/serial, supported population and BIOS/microcode compatibility
Owner/vendor socket installation procedure including orientation/keying, inspection, tool/torque, retention, TIM/heatsink and chassis restoration requirements
Qualified operator, ESD-safe bench, power isolation, maintenance/workload approval, KVM/OOB first-boot coverage and known-good recovery CPU/configuration
Exact firmware setup menu/page and expected CPU identity/topology fields, plus thermal/power/POST/log acceptance limits
execution_readiness_detail.input_owner: The platform/CPU owner supplies compatibility, population and expected firmware fields; the motherboard/vendor owner supplies the mechanical/thermal procedure; the lab owner supplies operator, ESD/tools, maintenance, first-power and recovery coverage.
safe_read_only_work_before_closure: Collect board/socket/BIOS/BMC/current-CPU identity, power/thermal health, active workload and preserved SEL/host baselines without changing state
Review CPU/board compatibility and installation documents offline; prepare the photo/setup-menu/health evidence manifest
prohibited_until_closed: Do not open the chassis, remove/install a CPU, touch socket contacts, apply TIM, operate retention hardware or power on after installation without the exact procedure and qualified operator
Do not force a part, guess compatibility/orientation/torque/TIM, clear logs, treat OS/BMC enumeration as a substitute for the firmware setup menu, or repeatedly reseat/power-cycle after failure
execution_readiness_detail.closure_verification: Two-person identity/compatibility check matches CPU, board, socket and BIOS; operator/tools/ESD/TIM/retention procedure and recovery are approved; the exact setup-menu evidence is defined; maintenance isolation, first-power limits and evidence collection are ready.

revision_candidate.test_name: CPU Socket Installation and Firmware Setup Recognition
revision_candidate.purpose: Install the approved CPU in the specified motherboard socket without mechanical or thermal damage and verify that the firmware setup menu reports the expected processor information.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: The exact server motherboard/socket revision and approved CPU package/stepping/BIOS combination in an ESD-safe service environment with qualified physical handling, KVM/OOB and recovery.
revision_candidate.target_scope: Only the owner-designated CPU and socket/population position. Firmware setup-menu recognition is mandatory; BMC/OS identity and health are supporting evidence rather than substitutes.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: SUT/board/socket identity; CPU model/stepping/package/serial and compatibility matrix; population/BIOS baseline; installation, tool/torque, retention, TIM/heatsink and chassis procedure; operator/ESD/maintenance approval; expected setup-menu fields; first-power/thermal limits; KVM/OOB and known-good recovery plan.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: No remote command performs installation. Preserve the pre-state; isolate power; have the qualified operator inspect, orient and install the exact CPU with the approved socket/TIM/retention sequence and no force; restore cooling/chassis; perform one controlled first power-on; enter the specified firmware setup page and record CPU identity/topology; then collect supporting POST, BMC/OS, thermal/power and log evidence.
revision_candidate.preconditions: Exact compatibility and package keying confirmed; socket/CPU visually clean and undamaged; correct tools/TIM/retention procedure; ESD and power isolation active; workload/window approved; cooling/chassis restoration checklist, setup-menu expectations, KVM/OOB and recovery owner ready; logs preserved.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: Compatibility approval and identities; before/after socket/CPU/retention/TIM/heatsink photos/records; operator/tool/ESD trace; first-power/POST timeline; named firmware setup page with expected CPU information; supporting BMC/OS identity; thermal/power and SEL/host deltas; restored chassis and recovery readiness.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: The exact motherboard/socket service manual, platform CPU support/population matrix, CPU package handling specification, thermal assembly procedure and owner-approved firmware setup fields.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: Never force or drag the package, touch/bend contacts, improvise orientation/tool/torque/TIM, power without completed cooling/retention, clear logs, repeat reseats blindly or claim success from physical fit or OS inventory alone.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: A qualified hardware operator performs all chassis/socket/CPU/TIM/cooling actions. The platform owner approves the exact CPU/board/BIOS match and first power-on; the end user adjudicates the setup and health evidence.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: Physical inspection, installation, retention, TIM/cooling assembly and chassis closure are manual. The agent may prepare evidence and collect approved read-only firmware/BMC/OS/health data around the operator action but cannot claim first-hand socket inspection.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: On pin/contact/package damage, abnormal fit, POST/boot/thermal/power failure or wrong recognition, remove power through the approved procedure, preserve the as-found physical/log state, avoid repeated reseating, and have the qualified owner restore the known-good CPU/configuration and verify health.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: Identity/compatibility uncertainty, socket or package damage/contamination, missing tool/TIM/torque procedure, abnormal fit or retention, incomplete cooling/chassis restoration, unavailable KVM/OOB/recovery, POST code or power/thermal anomaly, wrong setup-menu identity, new BMC/SEL fault or incomplete evidence.

identified_defects: The source defines compatibility only as CPU size and omits the exact CPU/socket/board/BIOS/thermal installation requirements.
V2 does not consistently distinguish mandatory firmware setup-menu recognition from optional supporting BMC/OS evidence.
The source's five/zero-minute timing cannot override safe installation and first-power procedures.
reason_for_change: Preserve V2's correct manual/safety conclusion while restoring the source-specific acceptance location: CPU information must be demonstrated in the approved firmware setup menu, not replaced by a convenient OS or BMC inventory query.

new_technical_evidence.title: Functionality row 74 source testcase
new_technical_evidence.supports: The procedure explicitly requires the setup menu to display CPU information after physical installation; the criterion also requires physical package/motherboard compatibility.

removed_ambiguities: Names the firmware setup menu as mandatory recognition evidence and BMC/OS data as supplemental.
Separates one controlled first power-on from uncontrolled repeat reseating or power cycling.
remaining_blockers: Physical execution waits for exact compatibility/install/thermal instructions, qualified operator, ESD/tools, first-power approval, setup-menu expectations and recovery.
objective_improvement_over_v2: V3 keeps V2's correct MANUAL ONLY and strict hardware controls but prevents the required firmware setup-menu check from being diluted into generic BIOS/BMC/OS inventory, and rejects the source timing as authorization to abbreviate safe installation or first boot.

agent_understanding_result.notes: The destructive high-risk manual contract and firmware-setup execution-location clarification are queued for isolated validation.

per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_purpose_fact: The source requires physical CPU installation plus CPU information displayed in the setup menu.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_v2_comparison: V2 correctly protects physical installation but groups several recognition sources; V3 makes firmware setup mandatory and other inventory supporting only.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_safety_evidence_decision: Only a qualified ESD-safe operator may install the exact compatible CPU; one controlled first power-on requires restored cooling, KVM/OOB and recovery, and no repeated blind reseat is allowed.
